Interface ReleasableRequestBody

All Known Subinterfaces:
AsyncHandlerBody
@Internal public interface ReleasableRequestBody
An AsyncRequestBody that a controller method or a request filter method was invoked with, as the server sees it: when the method completed, the server releases what its reads of the body left open, e.g. the elements it did not read or a file it was still writing, before the response is written or the filter chain continues, or, for a streamed response of a controller method, when its stream ended.

  • Method Details

    • releaseBody

      CompletionStage<Void> releaseBody()
      Release what the reads of the body left open: abort the reads that are still running, e.g. AsyncRequestBody.elements(Class), AsyncRequestBody.parts() or AsyncRequestBody.transferTo(java.nio.file.Path), and release the content they buffered or staged, the reads of its copies too. Releasing again does nothing more.
      Returns:
      Completes when released, exceptionally when releasing failed

    • releaseAfter

      static <T> ExecutionFlow<T> releaseAfter(ExecutionFlow<T> flow, ReleasableRequestBody body)
      Release the body once the flow of the method that was invoked with it completed, before the result of the flow is delivered: a failure to release fails a successful result, and is added as suppressed to a failure of the flow. A reactive flow stays reactive, and releases when it is subscribed to and completes.

      A flow that is cancelled before it completed, e.g. by a filter that stops waiting for the rest of the chain, releases the body when it is cancelled: nobody waits for that release, and its failure is logged. The body is released once, whether the flow completed, was cancelled, or both.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The result type
      Parameters:
      flow - The flow of the method
      body - The body the method was invoked with
      Returns:
      The flow, which completes once the body was released
